title: African motor professional captures guided vehicle photos while an insurer review interface organises the inspection evidence.
body_markdown:
Physical vehicle inspection can look controlled because an assessor sees the car. But a physical-only model also makes location and scheduling part of the workflow. The inspection cannot begin until the vehicle and assessor can meet.


A generic photo-upload link is not a better control. Incomplete, poorly framed, or unrelated images can simply move weak evidence online. The stronger alternative is structured capture, automated checks, and human review for the cases that need judgment.


## Better inspection starts with better evidence


[New York's vehicle-inspection standards](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/new-york/11-NYCRR-67.5) require defined vehicle views, VIN evidence, damage photographs, and retained records. In a different operating context,[AXA Mansard's digital inspection workflow](https://corporate.axamansard.com/axas-new-digital-tool-to-make-vehicle-inspection-fast-and-easy/) uses smartphone images, automated review, and reports that enter underwriting and claims processes.


Together, these examples point to the same operating principle: control comes from what the inspection captures, verifies, and preserves, not from physical presence alone.


A physical visit should remain available when evidence is uncertain, the loss is complex, or local rules require it. It does not need to be the default starting point for every case.


## Structure turns photos into an inspection record


A useful photo workflow should define what the customer captures and what happens when the evidence is incomplete. Depending on consent, local law, and the insurer's risk policy, the design may include:


- **Guided capture.** Request standard exterior views, close-ups of visible damage, VIN, odometer, and relevant documents.
- **Quality checks.** Flag blurred, dark, obstructed, or missing views before assessment.
- **Provenance checks.** Use live capture, timestamps, device signals, duplicate matching, or location data where appropriate.
- **One audit trail.** Keep original images, automated findings, reviewer actions, and the final decision together.


[Curacel Auto's documentation](https://docs.curacel.co/docs/guides/curacel-auto/) describes image capture, validation, preprocessing, damage analysis, reporting, and insurer review channels. An[independent report on AXA Mansard's deployment](https://leadership.ng/insurance-firm-debuts-digital-motor-inspection-tool/) also describes image submission, automated screening, documentation processing, and integration with insurer workflows.

## AI should triage evidence, not replace judgment


Computer vision can help organise images, surface visible damage, and prioritise review. It should not be presented as an infallible assessor.


Peer-reviewed research supports that caution. A[Heliyon vehicle-damage study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11298869/) identifies limited public datasets and gaps in environmental, lighting, and viewpoint coverage. The[IEEE-published CarDD research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.00945) likewise begins from the shortage of high-quality public data for car-damage detection.


The operating response is straightforward:


- **Automate repeatable checks.** Validate required views and structure the case file.
- **Escalate uncertainty.** Route low-confidence, complex, high-value, or suspicious cases to trained reviewers.
- **Measure disagreement.** Track overrides, missing evidence, rework, and reviewer-model differences.


That approach is also consistent with the[NAIC AI Model Bulletin](https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/cmte-h-big-data-artificial-intelligence-wg-ai-model-bulletin.pdf.pdf) and[NIST AI Risk Management Framework](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.100-1.pdf) , which emphasise testing, documentation, monitoring, governance, and defined human oversight.


## The African use case is operational, not theoretical


AXA Mansard has introduced smartphone-based inspection for comprehensive motor policy initiation, renewal documentation, and claims assessment in Nigeria. Both the[insurer's announcement](https://corporate.axamansard.com/axas-new-digital-tool-to-make-vehicle-inspection-fast-and-easy/) and[Leadership's reporting](https://leadership.ng/insurance-firm-debuts-digital-motor-inspection-tool/) describe the workflow and Curacel partnership.


That is evidence of deployment, not proof that every inspection should be automated or that the same results will apply to every insurer. The useful lesson is narrower: remote photo inspection can sit inside live underwriting and claims operations when the capture, review, and escalation steps are deliberately designed.


## The Takeaway


Structured photo-based inspection beats a physical-only process when it strengthens the evidence chain. Guided capture, quality checks, AI-assisted triage, durable records, and human escalation can make the workflow easier to start and easier to review without removing accountability.


The right question is not whether AI replaces physical inspection. It is which cases can proceed with structured evidence and which still need hands-on review.
